title: Introduced State Styling for UI Elements and Introduction Border Migration
description: Add a universal "introduced" styling state to UI elements: a pulsating border-thickness ring (not a spinning conic ring) in the highlight/primary color, triggered via a global `[data-introduced="true"]` attribute. Migrate the introduction (tour) system off its separate floating overlay ring div (ui/js/react/index.tsx ~4933-4935) so an introduced step is just a glass-veil cutout, and the anchored UI element itself displays the introduced styling by having the anchor DOM element stamped with data-introduced. Merge the IntroductionEmphasis enum: remove the "Highlight" variant entirely (greenfield, no back-compat) so only "None" and "Cutout" remain, with "Cutout" always implying the anchor pulses. The step's title/body text stays in the existing floating glass info box - only the ring migrates onto the element. Touches: ui/styling/js/ui.css (new keyframes + [data-introduced] rule), ui/js/react/index.tsx (hook stamping logic, emphasis handling, remove overlay div, extend in-file tests), framework/core/rs/lib.rs (remove Highlight variant), framework/core/js/generated/manifest.ts (regenerated via typegen), puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs (drop .emphasis(Highlight) calls), framework/product/os/dev/brand/entwerfen-mit-bestand.brand.ts (emphasis: "highlight" -> "cutout").
summary: Fixed the introduced-border-pulse default color: it was defaulting to --active-base (primary/red, the "active" semantic), but per the codebase's convention (resolveMeshStyle: highlighted uses tokenVar("secondary")) it should be the "highlighted" color. Changed the default in both the animated keyframes and the prefers-reduced-motion fallback to --color-secondary (teal #34d1bf). Verified visually and via computed getComputedStyle in the running mit-bestand aggregator dev server: the pulsing inset box-shadow on the introduced windowKind/panelTab anchors now renders as rgb(52, 209, 191) instead of the previous rgb(255, 52, 79).
